summary: Export writes the whole encrypted vault to one JSON file; import is replace-only and re-keys client-side under a freshly generated DEK, so an exported and a live vault never again share key material — both run through the same record-api validator, and import invalidates every other session in one transaction.

read.role: the session-invalidation pattern import must not be weaker than
the only screen this feature drives
button and error/confirmation-state conventions for the export/import screen, and the shell it renders inside

exportEndpoint.value: GET /api/export, requires X-Solvent-Request header despite being a GET; a plain top-level navigation returns 403 and writes nothing

exportFileShape.value: { format: "solvent-vault", formatVersion: 1, exportedAt, salt, kdf, wrappedDek, dekNonce, records: [{ recordId, recordType, accountId, schemaVersion, version, nonce, ciphertext }] } — no user identifier anywhere

exportRateLimit.value: default 5 per hour per user, operator config

importEndpoint.value: POST /api/import — one transaction: deletes every record belonging to the session user, replaces wrapped DEK, inserts the new set, invalidates every other session (keeps the importing one)

importIsReplaceOnly.value: no merge; a non-empty target vault requires a typed ERASE confirmation naming the record count to be destroyed

rekeySteps.value: 1) derive MK_file from the file's salt+kdf, unwrap DEK_file 2) decrypt every record with DEK_file and its own per-record AAD, abort whole import on any failure before sending anything 3) generate a new random 256-bit DEK_new 4) re-encrypt every record under DEK_new with a fresh nonce, version reset to 1, AAD rebuilt 5) wrap DEK_new under the current session's Master Key 6) POST the new wrapped DEK and re-encrypted records

serverImportValidation.value: same per-record validator as PUT /api/records (field-consistency included) plus: total payload size cap, per-record ciphertext size cap, record count cap, known recordType values, well-formed UUIDs, base64 decodes cleanly, accountId present exactly for snapshot (null otherwise, never empty string) and referencing an account in the same import, and version:1 enforced on every record regardless of what the client sent

userIdSource.value: the server assigns user_id from the session on every imported record; never reads one from the payload

sessionInvalidationScope.value: every other session for the user is invalidated in the same transaction as the import; the importing session survives — must not be weaker than a password change (account-settings.md), which changes strictly less

formatVersionRule.value: no formatVersion below 1 exists; an older version migrates client-side after decryption and before re-encryption, reusing the same per-type migration chain as lazy read migration (record-api.md); a newer/unknown formatVersion is rejected

profileReplacementIsSanctioned.value: import replaces the profile record too, which is the one sanctioned way the main currency changes — it does not violate account-settings.md's immutability rule because history is replaced together, staying internally consistent

fixtures: a populated vault (accounts + snapshots from manage-accounts.md and record-snapshot.md) to export, wipe, and re-import for the round-trip criterion
an export file from a different user account, for the cross-user vault-transfer criterion
a record taken from the source vault post-export and inserted directly into the destination's rows, for the re-key regression test
a file with one record's ciphertext altered by a single byte, for the abort-before-upload criterion
a formatVersion:1 fixture file, kept importable after the format advances, for the migration-chain regression test
a second live session for the importing user, for the session-invalidation criterion
a simulated DB failure mid-import, for the transactional-rollback criterion
focus: 'the wrapped DEK unwraps to a key that is not the file's DEK_file' must be asserted directly against the two key values, since a verbatim-restore bug would otherwise pass every other round-trip test in the list

the re-key regression test (source-vault record inserted into destination rows fails to decrypt) is the one that actually proves no shared key material — don't accept a passing round-trip test as a substitute for it
'nothing is uploaded until every record decrypts successfully' needs an assertion against actual network calls during a mid-decryption failure, not just the final error state
the export sensitivity warning must be shown before the download is triggered — assert ordering, not just presence

the session-invalidation criterion must show a create (new UUID, version 1) from the stale session lands as permanently unreadable ciphertext rather than silently succeeding — this is the scenario the spec calls out as the actual risk, not just 'the second session gets 401'
